Tensor Analysis – Practical 8 Solutions Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 8.1 The Christoffel symbols of the first kind can be expressed in terms of the metric tensor as follows: Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gik ∂xj + ∂gij ∂xk − ∂gkj ∂xi ) . This expression simplifies for orthogonal coordinate systems (those with gij = 0 when i ̸= j). Find the simplified expression for Γijk in the cases (1) i = j = k; (2) i = j ̸= k; (3) i ̸= j = k; (4) i, j, k are all distinct. Solution: (1) If i = j = k, then for fixed i (no summation convention), Γijk = Γiii = 1 2 ( ∂gii ∂xi + ∂gii ∂xi − ∂gii ∂xi ) = 1 2 ∂gii ∂xi . (2) If i = j ̸= k, then likewise Γijk = Γiik = 1 2 ( ∂gii ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xi − ∂gik ∂xi ) = 1 2 ∂gii ∂xk . (3) If i ̸= j = k then Γijk = Γijj = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xj + ∂gij ∂xj − ∂gjj ∂xi ) = − 1 2 ∂gjj ∂xi , as gij = 0 for i ̸= j. (d) If i, j, k are all distinct, then Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) = 0. 1

2 8.2 [See lecture] We have seen in Practical 5 spherical coordinates (x1, x2, x3) = (r, ϕ, θ), the metric tensors are g11 = 1, g22 = r2, g33 = r2 sin 2 ϕ, and the other components of the metric tensor are trivial. Find the Christoffel symbols of the first and second kind. Solution: We have a formula for Γijk in terms of the metric tensors: Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . As the only non-constant gij are g22 = r2 and g33 = r2 sin 2 ϕ, the only non-zero partial derivatives ∂gij ∂xk are ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂r2 ∂r = 2r, ∂g33 ∂x1 = ∂(r2 sin 2 ϕ) ∂r = 2r sin 2 ϕ, ∂g33 ∂x2 = ∂(r2 sin 2 ϕ) ∂ϕ = 2r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ. So, we conclude that the only possibly non-zero Christoffel symbols are the ones with indices • 1,2,2, or • 1,3,3, or • 2,3,3, in some order. Thus Γ122 = 1 2 ( ∂g12 ∂x2 + ∂g12 ∂x2 − ∂g22 ∂x1 ) = − 1 2 ∂g22 ∂x1 = − 1 2 · 2r = −r, Γ212 = Γ221 = 1 2 ∂g22 ∂x1 = 1 2 · 2r = r, Γ133 = − 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x1 = − 1 2 · 2r sin 2 ϕ = −r sin 2 ϕ, Γ313 = Γ331 = 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x1 = 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x1 = 1 2 · 2r sin 2 ϕ = r sin 2 ϕ, Γ233 = − 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x2 = − 1 2 · (2r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ) = −r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ, Γ323 = Γ332 = 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x2 = 1 2 · (2r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ) = r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ Γijk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k.

Recall that in orthogonal coordinate systems gii = 1 gii and gij = 0 if i ̸= j. Thus g11 = 1, g22 = 1 r2 , g33 = 1 r2 sin 2 ϕ . Applying to the formula, we see that Γ 1 22 = g11Γ122 = −r, Γ 2 12 = Γ 2 21 = g22Γ212 = 1 r2 · r = 1 r , Γ 1 33 = g11Γ133 = −r sin 2 ϕ, Γ 3 13 = Γ 3 31 = g33Γ313 = 1 r2 sin 2 ϕ · (r sin 2 ϕ) = 1 r , Γ 2 33 = g22Γ233 = 1 r2 · (−r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ) = − sin ϕ cos ϕ, Γ 3 23 = Γ 3 32 = g33Γ323 = 1 r2 sin 2 ϕ · (r2 sin ϕ cos ϕ) = cot ϕ Γijk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k. 8.3 Consider the 2D coordinates (x1, x2) = (ρ, θ), in which the position vector r is given by r = ρ 2 cos(2θ) i1 + ρ 2 sin(2θ) i2, where i1, i2 are the usual 2-dimensional Cartesian basis vectors. (1) Find the corresponding basis vectors e1 and e2. (2) Find the covariant metric tensor gij and give your answer as a 2 × 2 matrix. Using the fact that the basis e1, e2 is orthogonal, find the contravariant metric tensor gij. (3) Find all Christoffel symbols Γijk of the first kind. (4) Find all Christoffel symbols Γi jk of the second kind.

4 Solution: (1) We know that ei = ∂r ∂xi . Thus e1 = ∂r ∂x1 = ∂r ∂ρ = 2ρ cos(2θ) i1 + 2ρ sin(2θ) i2, e2 = ∂r ∂x2 = ∂r ∂θ = −2ρ2 sin(2θ) i1 + 2ρ 2 cos(2θ) i2. (2) By definition, gij = ei · ej. Thus g11 = (2ρ cos(2θ) 2ρ sin(2θ) ) · (2ρ cos(2θ) 2ρ sin(2θ) ) = 4ρ2 cos2(2θ) + 4ρ 2 sin 2(2θ) = 4ρ2, g12 = g21 = (2ρ cos(2θ) 2ρ sin(2θ) ) · (−2ρ2 sin(2θ) 2ρ2 cos(2θ) ) = −4ρ3 cos(2θ) sin(2θ) + 4ρ3 cos(2θ) sin(2θ) = 0, g22 = (−2ρ2 sin(2θ) 2ρ2 cos(2θ) ) · (−2ρ2 sin(2θ) 2ρ2 cos(2θ) ) = 4ρ4 sin 2(2θ) + 4ρ 4 cos2(2θ) = 4ρ4. Note that since gij = 0 when i ̸= j, this is system is orthogonal. Thus, we can use the formula gii = 1 gii . We obtain g11 = 1 4ρ2 , g22 = 1 4ρ4 . By definition of orthogonal, we have g12 = g21 = 0. In matrix notation, we have G = [gij] = ( 4ρ2 0 0 4ρ4 ) , [gij] = ( 1 4ρ2 0 0 1 4ρ4 ) . (3) Recall that (1) Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . Since G = [gij] = ( 4ρ2 0 0 4ρ4 ) ,

(4) To find the Christoffel symbols of second kind Γi jk we use the formula Γ i jk = giℓΓℓkj = gi1Γ1kj + gi2Γ2kj. Since [gij] = ( 1 4ρ2 0 0 1 4ρ4 ) . Γ1 11 = g11Γ111 = 1 4ρ2 · 4ρ = 1 ρ , Γ1 12 = Γ 1 21 = g11Γ112 = 1 4ρ2 · 8ρ 3 = 2ρ, Γ2 11 = g22Γ211 = 1 4ρ4 · (−8ρ3) = − 2 ρ , Γ i kj = 0, for all other values of i, j, k.

(1) Find the corresponding basis vectors e1, e2, and e3. (2) Find the covariant metric tensor gij and the contravariant metric tensor gij. Give your final answer as 2 × 2 matrices. (3) Find all Christoffel symbols Γijk of the first kind. (4) Find all Christoffel symbols Γi jk of the second kind. Solution: (1) We know that ei = ∂r ∂xi . Thus e1 = ∂r ∂x1 = ∂r ∂x = 2x i1 + 2y i2, e2 = ∂r ∂x2 = ∂r ∂y = −2y i1 + 2x i2 e3 = ∂r ∂x3 = ∂r ∂t = i3. (2) By definition, gij = ei · ej. By definition of orthogonal, we also have gij = 0, whenever i ̸= j. (3) To compute the Christoffel symbols of first kind, we use the following formula: Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) .
